title: Ad-Hoc Runtime Class-Loading Plugin System
pattern: Loading arbitrary dynamically compiled shared libraries (`.so` or `.dll` files) at runtime using manual memory offsets, solely to toggle localized system configurations or trivial business rule variants.
why_bad: It introduces critical security vulnerabilities (binary hijacking), degrades compiler cross-module optimizations (LTO), and causes runtime segmentation faults or panics if symbols are missing.
detection: The direct use of unsafe dynamic library loaders (like the `libloading` crate) inside core domain execution pathways to dispatch variants.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. True microkernel architectures or extensible platforms (like Web browsers) where dynamic module loading is a fundamental requirement.
source: Mark Richards, Neal Ford - _Fundamentals of Software Architecture_ An Engineering Approach_ (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 12 "Microkernel Architecture Style"; Joshua Kerievsky - _Refactoring to Patterns_ (2004, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 7.
